dedupe_keys.name: cpuc fire threat map and high fire threat district hftd for power line fire safety in california

description: The CPUC Fire-Threat Map and the High Fire-Threat District (HFTD) map show where California overhead power lines and nearby communication facilities face elevated risk of igniting and spreading wildfire, and therefore where stricter fire-safety rules in General Order 95 apply. The Safety and Enforcement Division of the California Public Utilities Commission built the statewide map from Fire Map 1, an agnostic CAL FIRE map of areas with strong winds, abundant dry vegetation and other conditions associated with the catastrophic 2007 power line fires, adopted in 2016, and combined it with the USFS-CAL FIRE Tier 1 tree-mortality High Hazard Zones to form the HFTD. The final map was adopted on 19 January 2018. The page also documents the interim FRAP, SDG&E and Reax maps that preceded it. Access: high-resolution PDF maps, a zip archive of native GIS files and a GIS web app viewer, all downloaded from the page without registration. Licence and cost: free; no licence text is shown. Caveats: a regulatory zoning map fixed in 2018 that does not represent asset-level fragility or current fuel conditions. It suits wildfire exposure screening of overhead lines and public safety power shutoff studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
